content:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, iPhones and iPads have featured a Notification Center, which serves as a centralised, chronological place to view alerts from various apps.

Starting from iOS 27, Apple has made major changes to the way users open Notification Center on iPhones and iPads.

iOS 27 is currently in beta, and the behaviour has varied slightly between the first two beta versions. However, both the third developer beta and the first public beta indicate this change will officially roll out this autumn.

Siri AI takes over most of the swipe gestures from the top edge of iPhones and iPads

On iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the default way to open Notification Center remains unchanged. However, enabling Siri AI will change one important swipe gesture on iPhones and iPads.

When Siri AI is enabled, one way to summon it is by swiping down from the centre of the top edge of an iPhone or iPad screen. Previously, this gesture was used to open Notification Center.

With Siri AI enabled, you can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner. Notifications will now animate in from the top-left corner. This is a way to direct users' attention to the smaller operating area of Notification Center.

Apple has placed extremely strong emphasis on accessibility to Siri AI in iOS 27. Most of the top edge is used to summon the all-new Siri experience.

The last time Apple modified access to Notification Center was with the iPhone X, when Control Center was changed from a bottom swipe to a swipe down from the top-right corner. Apple subsequently extended this experience uniformly to all devices.

Notifications are now located in the top-left corner

Top comments posted by mz4srmsr

I've always swiped down from the left corner to check my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe down from the middle 😂 Guess I should be fine then?

Now it's Notification Center's turn to be "pushed into a corner." Especially in iPadOS 27 beta 1, the area above the home screen app icons is almost entirely used for summoning Siri AI. If you turn off the display of AM/PM or the date, the area for opening Notification Center will shrink even further.

Apple made improvements in iPadOS 27 beta 2, making the left and right sides more balanced. Each side is roughly the width of two rows of app icons—the left side for Notification Center, the right side for Control Center, and the rest is used for summoning Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it'll take time to judge whether this change is worthwhile. During this period, initial opinions on Apple's all-new Siri AI system have generally been quite positive. Getting used to "Siri finally being good" will probably also take some time.

iOS 27 is currently available in developer and public beta versions. The official version is expected to launch in early September.
